verdicts.evidence: framework-selector.md:202 — "  primary: {framework name and version}"; framework-selector.md:169 — "**Framework:** {framework name and version}"
verdicts.reasoning: REFUTED as a contradiction. Both quotes verified. It is true that the block key is `primary`, not `framework` — but that is not the guide and the skill disagreeing about behavior. `primary` is defined in the skill as literally '{framework name and version}', §2 carries the same value under the label '**Framework:**' (line 169), and the KICKOFF sentence is 'Keep system_type, framework and model_provider from that block' — plain-English 'the framework', not a literal key lookup. The very next dispatch block at KICKOFF.md:425 confirms the intended reading: 'Give it the framework name and version, the system_type and the model_provider framework-selector just returned.' No orchestrator following this ends up with the wrong value, so there is no behavioral disagreement to fix — this is incidental phrasing, which the classification rules exclude. The sentence's actual function — telling the operator which three values to carry into the downstream dispatches — is load-bearing and should be KEPT as written.
